caseno: Death Reference No. 51 of 2010 with Criminal Appeal No. 5359 of 2010 with Jail Appeal No. 238 of 2010.
lawyer:
MA Mannan Mohon, DAG with Md. Aminur Rahman Chowdhury and Kazi Bazlur Rashid, AAGs—For the State 
Sarwar Ahmed, with Sudhendu Kumar Biswas, Advocates—For the Condemned-Prisoner
parties:
State ----- Petitioner
VS
Mizanur Rahman ----- Condemned-Prisoner.
full_judgment:
4. After the close of evidence from the side of the prosecution all the three accused persons were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. At that time also they pleaded not guilty and declined to adduce any evidence in support of their case. 

 5. The learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Jhalakathi thereafter, considering the evidence on record found the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman guilty under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and the remaining accused persons namely Delwara Begum and Giashuddin not guilty of the charge brought against them under section 11(ka)/30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and consequently acquitted them therefrom by his judgment and order dated 11-8-2010. 

 8. The learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the condemned-prisoner Md. Mizanur Rahman in support of the defence case during their submissions submits that the learned Judge of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Jhalakathi at the time of disposal of the original case committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that during trial of the original case the prosecution has failed to adduce any independent, disinterested eye witnesses of the case in presence of whom the alleged occurrence of killing the deceased was held. The learned trial judge on the basis of surmise and conjecture without proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law decided that the husband of the deceased Selina Akter for want of dower money amounting to Taka 20,000 killed his wife by smothering. The learned Advocate further submits that there is no iota of evidence in favour of the prosecution that the condemned-prisoner ever claimed any dowry from his wife or from the parents of his wife Selina Akter and apart from this; the preparation of inquest report by the Sub-Inspector of Police is barred by law as provided in section 174(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure as a Sub-Inspector of Police or Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police, below the rank of Inspector is not empowered to prepare Inquest Report of the dead body. Besides this; there is no averment within the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses that for want of "যৌতুক" the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman tortured his wife Selina Akter and killed her by smothering. The learned Advocate also submits that in the instant case the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman is entitled to get benefit of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act as all the charge-sheeted witnesses not examined in this case to substantiate the case of the prosecution. Besides this; the examination of the condemned-prisoner under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is faulty and condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman, who is the appellant of Criminal Appeal No. 5359 of 2010 and Jail Appeal No. 238 of 2010 has been prejudiced during examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The learned Advocates with regard to this has drawn our attention on the number of witnesses examined who were 6 in numbers. During examination of the accused despite the prosecution witnesses were 6 but the learned trial Judge instead of 6 PWs mentioned that 5 prosecution witnesses have been examined from the side of the prosecution who has supported the case and deposed against the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman. The learned Advocates argued that it is an apparent mistake of facts which cannot be ignored and such sort of illegalities has visited the entire proceedings of the case. The learned Advocates lastly submits that the learned trial Judge with-out proper attention and evaluation of the evidence on record in a very hasty manner decided the merit of the case in favour of the prosecution and convicted the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman sentencing him to death penalty and in fact; there is no legal evidence by dint of which it can be held that the condemned-prisoner committed any offence punishable under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to he set aside and the death reference is liable to be rejected. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocates of the condemned-prisoner the learned Deputy Attorney-General opposing the submissions controverted the argument advanced from the side of the learned counsels of the defence and submits that the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Jhalakathi during trial of the original case as well as disposal of the same committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Deputy Attorney General further submits that the learned trial Judge at the time of deciding the merit of the case properly appreciated the relevant laws and assessed the evident on records in its true perspective and thereafter complying all the legal formalities of criminal trial decided the merit of the case in favour of the prosecution and against the defence. There are sufficient number of disinterested, competent, credible witnesses who in a voice testified that in-between the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman and the deceased Selina Akter marriage ceremony was legally solemnized and they lived together as husband and wife in the dwelling but of the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman situated in village-Paschim Chandkathi under Police Station and District-Jhalakathi and it is proved beyond all shadow of doubt by credible, tangible evidence that the wife of the condemned-prisoner Selina Akter met with her death in the residence of her husband Mizanur Rahman. The learned DAG in this context; referred some decisions of this Court and our Apex Court and argued that, it is a decided matter that it is the husband who is to explain and answer as to why and how his wife Selina Akter met with her death; which was no doubt unnatural in  nature. The learned DAG submits that the husband of the deceased in this case has totally failed to discharge his onus in giving any reply or explanation whatsoever as to why and how his wife died in his residence. The learned Deputy Attorney General further submits that the ejahar of this case is very much clear which has been marked as Exhibit-2 disclosing that for want of dower money the occurrence was held and besides this; it is within the charge sheet, charge and examination of the accused under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure that the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman for want of "যৌতুক" killed his wife brutally. Therefore, it is very much within the prosecution case that for want of dower money the occurrence of killing the deceased Selina Akter was held. Inasmuch as; the very case and it's proceedings (trial) do proceed for murder for want of dower money the witnesses did not feel any necessity to mention the ward dowry with-in their deposition. The prosecution witnesses one after another corroborated each-other with regard to the positive case of the prosecution and thus dowry is implied in the testimonies of the witnesses for which the husband of the deceased tortured his wife and at a stage of that; killed his wife Selina in his residence by smothering and, as such, there are sufficient ingredients of section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman AM, 2000 against the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman. Secondly, the learned Deputy Attorney General has drawn our attention over the provisions laid down in section 174(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure wherein there is a clear proviso-clause, from where; it is clear that the act of preparation of inquest report of the dead body was not at all illegal by the Sub-Inspector of Police below the rank of Inspector of the concerned police station. Apart from this; during examination of the accused under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure there was no such illegality for which the condemned-prisoner can be prejudiced. In fact; PW 5 the PM done doctor practically did not give any complete decision as to the cause of death and as it was an incomplete testimony of prosecution witness No. 5 during examination of the accused under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the learned trial judge ousted the witness No. 5 and mentioned the number of the witnesses who deposed in favour of the prosecution as 5 (five) instead of 6 (six). The learned Deputy Attorney General lastly submits in support of the prosecution case as well as the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence that in the instant case; the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Jhalakathi in presence of the condemned-prisoner examined all the witnesses and the trial was concluded legally and thereafter considering all the evidence on record, facts and circumstances of the case on the assessment of all legal evidence awarded death penalty to the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman in presence of sufficient ingredients under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 11-8-2010 should be upheld and the reference is liable to be accepted. 

 10. In view of the aforesaid submissions made from the sides of the learned Advocates of both sides, to arrive at a conclusive decision as to guilt of the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman let us now scan and evaluate the evidence adduced from the side of the prosecution and other materials on record. 

 19. During cross-examination from the side of the defence this witness testified at a stage that his homestead is situated to the northern side of the place of occurrence home-stead. PW 4 denied the suggestion put before him from the side of the defence that to grab the property of Mizanur Rahman in collusion with the witnesses he deposed falsely before the Court. This witness also denied that his evidence is not correct. 

 24. Scrutinizing the evidence on record it transpires that the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman along with co-accused Delwara Begum and Mizanur's brother Giasuddin faced the trial all along and accordingly; charge was framed against them by the trial Judge separately. Against the condemned-prisoner Md. Mizanur Rahman the charge was framed under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman AM, 2000 on 13-8-2006 and that charge was such that he (Mizanur Rahman) in collusion with the co-accused for want of dowry in between 10-00 pm (of 3-1-2006) to 7-00 am (of 4-1-2006) killed his wife in his residence after tiding her neck by a scarf, at which due to suffocation his wife the deceased Selina Akter met with her death and thereby the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman committed the offence punishable under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. Side by side; the co-accused Delwara Begum and Giashuddin were charged under section 11(ka)/30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 for abetment. The trial judge after trial finding the co-accused not guilty of the charge lavelled against them for want of tangible evidence acquitted them therefrom and finding sufficient convincing legal evidence against the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman found him guilty under section 11(ka) of the aforesaid Ain and passed the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence. It further transpires from the evidence on record that the witnesses were presented from the side of the prosecution in presence of the condemned-prisoner and those witnesses were cross-examined thoroughly from the side of Mizanur Rahman and thereafter at the close of evidence the trial Judge examined the condemned-prisoner Mizanur under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 26. In this context; it is to be mentioned here that the chemical Examiner after his examination submitted his report vide Report No. 3443. It is also apparent from the face of the record that Dr. Md. Nowsher Ali along with Dr. Ratan Kumar Dhali as to the actual cause of death consulting the report of chemical Examiner opined on 31-3-2006 that in their opinion the death was due to asphyxia resulting from strangulation which was ant mortem and homicidal in nature. Section 509A of the Code of Criminal Procedure dispensed with the necessity of formal proof of the Expert's Report. The proposition of law is such that the said report may be used as evidence dispensing with the attendance of the concerned doctor/Expert. Moreover; as the factum of murder has been proved by four witnesses of the place of occurrence locality the postmortem report is not absolutely essential as corroborative evidence. It is evident from the materials on record that the deceased of this case died because of smothering not for any other reason. The witnesses Nos. 2, 3 and 4 in a voice corroborated the case of the prosecution as to the death of the deceased Selina Akther. 

 28. Having gone through the evidence on record along with the connected papers and materials on record we find that the police officer after taking investigation of the case which was endorsed upon him by the officer-in-Charge of Jhalakathi police station visited the place of occurrence residence which belong to the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman. It is from the sketch map and it's index which has been marked as Exhibit-5 and 6 respectively that the place of occurrence is the homestead of Mizanur Rahman in where his wife met with her unnatural death. In the sketch map 'Avis the place of occurrence which is no doubt the homestead of Md. Mizanur Rahman. Keeping ahead the submissions of the learned counsels analyzing the evidence it is evident that the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman from the very beginning of starting the evidence with effect from 23-1-2007 to ending till 5-7-2010 was present in the court-room personally and in presence of the condemned-prisoner himself the entire proceedings were concluded from its beginning and the witnesses were examined in the open court in front of the condemned-prisoner. In this context; it is to be remembered that in the pretext of non-reading of all evidence/deposition of the witnesses, the trial would not be vitiated; if there is no question of prejudice due to any flow in the examination of the accused under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Here in this case; it appears that all the prosecution witnesses were cross-examined at-length on behalf of the condemned-prisoner and thorough cross-examination on the entire case of the defence, a lot of questions as well as bundle of suggestions were put to the witnesses. Hence; the condemned-prisoner along with his co-accused were fully aware or in the know about the prosecution case and the evidence from start to finish, who deposed to substantiate the case of the prosecution. They had therefore, no difficulty to follow the proceedings and after closer of the evidence of the prosecution they were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The learned trial Judge has drawn their proper attention stating that they have heard the evidence in details and they were asked if they had anything to say. The reply was simply that they are innocent. In this circumstances, it cannot be said that any miscarriage or failure of justice has been caused and, as such, there arises no question of prejudice of the condemned-prisoner in the trial held against him or during his examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. With regard to this; their lordships has given a land-mark pragmatic directive in the case of Abdur Razzaque vs State, 28 DLR (AD) 35 wherein it was held that the purpose of section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to inform the accused of the case about the incriminating evidence which has come against him from the side of the prosecution. If such evidence is within the knowledge of the accused, there is no question of prejudice. This court in the case of Zakir Hossain vs State, 55 DLR 137 retain the same view as cited above. 

 30. On critical analysis of the evidence it further appears that in this case; the local witnesses are witness No. 1 the informant, witness No. 2 Liton Kazi, witness No. 3 Faruk Sarder and witness No. 4 Md. Belayet Hossain, who has established beyond all shadow of doubt that the wife of the condemned-prisoner, the victim girl Selina Akter met with her death which was unnatural in nature in the residence of her husband in the night following 3-1-2006. It is also established that the condemned-prisoner and the deceased Selina Akter were living together at the time of occurrence as husband and wife in their residence the PO but situated at Paschim Chandkathi under Police Station and District-Jhalakathi. The prosecution witnesses in a voice testified before the court that they found the dead body of the deceased in the morning of 4-1-2006 in the residence of the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman and one of the local witnesses PW 3 Md. Faruk Sarder in his testimony categorically testified that after the occurrence in the morning of 4-1-2006 the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman and his mother Delwara Begum left their homestead. There is no explanation whatsoever from the side of the condemned-prisoner as to how and why his wife met with her unnatural death in his dwelling hut. It is a decided matter in our jurisdiction that, it is the husband; who shall have to explain as to how and why his wife met with her death in his residence. But in the instant case; as we have already spelt out that the condemned-prisoner remained silent all along as to the cause of unnatural death of his wife. 

 32. Law enjoins that in a wife killing case it is quite natural that there could be no eye-witness of the occurrence apart from the inmates of the house who may refuse to tell the truth. The neighbors may not also come forward to depose about the prosecution case; and that is why there is a necessity to rely on the circumstantial evidence. 

 33. Having gone through the materials on record we find that by sufficient credible cogent (both oral and circumstantial) evidence it is proved that the wife died in the house of her husband. Be that as it may; there exist strong presumptive value that in the hands of husband the wife met with her death. This very findings have got every support in the case of Bias Hussain vs State, 54 DLR (AD) 78 where in their lordships held, when a wife met with an unnatural death in custody of the husband and also in his house the husband is to explain under what circumstance the wife met with her death. 

 34. On meticulous assessment of evidence along with the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence; it appears that the learned trial Judge relying upon several decisions of this Court arrived at a decision from the testimonies of witnesses Nos. 1-4 and from the surrounding circumstances of this case which was prevailing at the time of occurrence stating that the wife of Mizanur Rahman the deceased of this case Selina Akter met with her unnatural death in the dwelling but of her husband Mizanur's homestead and Mizanur Rahman at the time of occurrence was living with his wife Selina Akter. 

 35. In the instant case; no where the defence have any case or any such suggestion that at the time of occurrence the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman as not in his residence rather he was outside of that and the husband and wife were not living together in their dwelling house. The very circumstantial evidence as it appears is a strong incriminating evidence against the condemned-prisoner to connect him in the offence of killing his wife Selina Akter, In the case of State vs Md. Sadequl Islam Tusar, 63 DLR (AD) 134, their lordships held in connection with the offence punishable under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 that, inasmuch as the husband of the deceased is to explain as to how the victim wife met with her death; the minimum onus of proof lies on the prosecution that at the relevant time the husband was present in the house or was residing with his wife in the same place of occurrence residence. 

 36. In this case; analyzing the material evidence on record we find that the prosecution have successfully discharged their onus that the husband Mizanur Rahman was residing in his residence with his wife Selina Akter on the date of occurrence and Selina in the residence of her husband met with her unnatural death when the husband and wife were living together as husband and wife in the same dwelling-hut which was the place of occurrence. 

 37. The learned trial Judge in his findings and decision rightly pointed out after thorough discussions over the evidence on record and after proper assessment of the same in its true perspective that it is the husband of the victim Selina Akter who has killed his wife in his dwelling house and thereby he committed the offence of killing his wife by smothering. With regard to this; on close reading of the judgment and order of conviction and sentence it appears that the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Jhalakathi vividly discussed and evaluated the evidence which are oral, documentary and circumstantial and thereafter arrived at a concrete decision as to the guilt of the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman who for want of dower money murdered his wife Selina Akter brutally in his residence situated in village-Paschim Chandkathi under Jhalakathi police station. 

 38. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above before parting, I must observe that the facts, circumstances and the nature of the case has properly been evaluated before awarding death sentence by the learned trial Judge. The way in which the condemned-prisoner Md. Mizanur Rahman committed murder of his ill-fated wife Selina Akter is no doubt shocking to the conscience of everybody and, as such, we find nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court. Hence, the aforesaid guilt of the accused deserve the highest degree of punishment which is the death penalty. Besides this; the legal evidence as laid down from the side of the prosecution is convincing with the conviction and sentence of death penalty as imposed upon the condemned-prisoner Mizanur Rahman under this reference by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Jhalakathi. We have found nothing in the circumstances of the case and in the conduct of the condemned-prisoner to take lenient view in the matter of the sentence despite our best concern to temper justice with mercy.
